summary: Renate Syed is an Indologist who earned her doctorate at the University of Munich (~1976-1982) under Dieter Schlingloff, Friedrich Wilhelm, and Gritli von Mitterwallner. She was attested as a Privatdozentin at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities in 2026.

Renato Dávalos works in Indology and philosophy, having studied at UAM, UNAM, El Colegio de México, and the University of Cologne (Ph.D. 2019-2023). He served as a Researcher Fellow at the CNRS from 2023 to 2026.
Renjo Akamatsu (1841-1919) was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Chō Sanshū and held a post at Ryukoku University.

Renshan Yang (1837-1911) was a Buddhist studies scholar who founded the Jinling Scriptural Press (1897), Jetavana Hermitage (1908), and the Buddhist Research Society (1910), serving as its head in 1910.
René Daumal (1908-1944) was active in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the Lycée Henri-IV (~1925-1927) and the Sorbonne (~1927-1929).

René Fohalle (1899-1984), a linguist and Indologist, studied at the University of Liège, Athénée royal Thil Lorrain Verviers, and under Antoine Meillet, Émile Benveniste, and Joseph Mansion. He was Professor ordinarius at the University of Liège (1929-1969).
René Gothóni is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Helsinki (~1970-1982), where he became Emeritus Professor in 2016.

René Grousset (1885-1952) was a historian, Sinologist, and Iranian/Central Asian specialist who studied at the University of Montpellier. He held posts at the Guimet Museum, Musée Cernuschi, École du Louvre, INALCO, and the Musée du Louvre.

René Guénon (1886-1951) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at the Robert-Badinter School Complex, Collège-lycée Jacques-Decour, École Polytechnique, the Sorbonne, the University of Paris, and under Sylvain Lévi.

René de Nebesky-Wojkowitz (1923-1959) worked in Tibetology, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at Charles University, Humboldt University, SOAS, LSE, and the University of Vienna, where he habilitated and became a PD in 1955, later serving at Weltmuseum Wien.

Reo Fortune (1903-1979) studied at Victoria University of Wellington and the University of Cambridge under Thomas Callan Hodson (~1926-1927). He later held a post at the University of Cambridge (~1947-1970).

Reuben Burrow (1747-1792) was active in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as an assistant astronomer and schoolmaster at the Royal Observatory, Greenwich (~1770-1773), taught at the Tower of London, and was a member of The Asiatic Society (~1784-1792).

Reuven Kahane (1931-2003), who worked in Indology and sociology, completed his Ph.D. under Neil Smelser at UC Berkeley (~1966-1970). He was a Lecturer and then Professor of Sociology and Anthropology at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1970-2001).

Revilo Pendleton Oliver (1908-1994), an Indologist and classicist, studied at Pomona College and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign under William Abbott Oldfather. He taught at Illinois from 1945, serving as Professor of Classics (1953-1977).
Rewa Prasad Dwivedi (1935-2021) was an Indology scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University and served there as Head of Sahityavidya (~1977-1995).

Rewata Dhamma (1929-2004) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his BA, MA, and PhD at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1956-1967) and also earned a doctorate from Banaras Hindu University (1956-1967).

Ria Kloppenborg (1945-2003) studied Buddhist studies, Indology, and religion at Leiden and Utrecht (Ph.D. under Jan Gonda). She held posts at Utrecht University (1970-1975; Professor of History of Religions, 1988) and the University of Groningen (1979-1988).

Richa Negi works in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied at Kurukshetra University and MNNIT Allahabad, and was attested as Head of Department at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts in 2026.

Richard A. Hutch is a religious studies scholar who studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. He held academic posts at Southern Illinois University Carbondale (~1974-1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978-2010).

Richard B. Mahoney works in Buddhist studies and computational fields. He earned his Master of Arts at the University of Canterbury under Paul Harrison by 2002 and held an attested post there in 2001.
